Overview & Responsibilities
Background
Under the framework of its Multi-Year Rule of Law for Stability Programme , and with financial support from the Government of the Kingdom of the Netherlands , the International Development Law Organization (IDLO) will implement the Damal Programme Phase II (2026-2030) in Somalia and Somaliland. Building on the achievements, lessons learned, and institutional partnerships established under the first phase of the Damal Programme, Phase II seeks to strengthen social cohesion, improve public trust in justice and security institutions, and enhance equitable access to justice for vulnerable populations. The programme recognises that effective, accessible, and accountable justice systems are fundamental to peaceful societies, conflict prevention, inclusive governance, and sustainable development. By strengthening both formal and community-based justice mechanisms and promoting collaboration among justice and security institutions, the programme aims to contribute to a more responsive, inclusive, and resilient justice sector.
Damal II will be implemented primarily in underserved, rural, urban, and conflict-affected areas where justice gaps, insecurity, and social exclusion remain significant barriers to peace and development. The programme adopts an integrated approach that combines Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), reconciliation, justice-security coordination, legal aid, referral mechanisms, community engagement, institutional capacity development, research, and evidence-based programming . It also places particular emphasis on strengthening access to justice for women, girls, internally displaced persons (IDPs), minority clans, persons with disabilities, youth, and other vulnerable justice seekers who continue to face disproportionate barriers in accessing fair and timely justice services. The programme is structured around three mutually reinforcing intermediate outcomes:

•
Intermediate Outcome 1 : Vulnerable groups have improved access to gender-responsive ADR and reconciliation services.

•
Intermediate Outcome 2 : Justice-security coordination mechanisms in urban and conflict-affected areas are more responsive, trusted, and effective.

•
Intermediate Outcome 3: Vulnerable justice seekers with cases beyond ADR mandates receive timely, coordinated, gender-responsive, and rights-based justice services through an integrated referral system.

To ensure a strong, evidence-based, and context-responsive start-up, the Damal Programme Phase II will commence with a preparatory phase , designed to refine implementation strategies, validate assumptions underpinning the Theory of Change, strengthen institutional coordination, and ensure interventions respond to evolving political, legal, security, and social dynamics.
A central feature of the above will be an extensive programme of stakeholder consultations across all programme target locations. As part of the consultations, IDLO will engage representatives from the justice sector, executive institutions, legislative bodies, the judiciary, prosecution services, law enforcement agencies, traditional dispute-resolution actors, civil society organisations, academia, women's organisations, youth representatives, community leaders, development partners, and local communities. These consultations will facilitate agreement on implementation priorities, coordination mechanisms, referral pathways, institutional roles, and approaches for strengthening access to justice within different geographic and institutional contexts.

Under the overall supervision of the IDLO Field Programme Manager, and in close collaboration with the Damal II Programme Team and IDLO technical teams, consortium partners, and relevant government counterparts, the Consultant shall design and undertake a comprehensive Baseline Assessment and Legal Analysis for the Damal Programme Phase II (2026-2030).

title: Software Engineer, Host Assurance
description:
About the Team

Security is foundational to OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Security organization protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products by building and operating deeply technical systems that must work reliably at massive scale. Our work underpins OpenAI’s commitments around safety, privacy, and security across research, products, and emerging platforms.

The Host Assurance team exists to make bare metal and VMs dependable & scalable foundations for OpenAI: secure by default, verifiable in practice, and resilient across providers and operating models. We operate at the trust boundary between hardware and cloud-scale orchestration, ensuring that hosts are eligible to safely run workloads with predictable security properties and auditability.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Software Engineer, Host Assurance to build and operate the services, APIs, and host software that establish and maintain trust in our compute infrastructure. You will own production software from design and implementation through testing, rollout, observability, and operation. Your work will support capabilities such as machine identity, certificate issuance and enrollment, secure bootstrap, and host attestation across bare-metal and VM environments.

Success in this role requires strong technical judgment, the ability to reason across software and host-system boundaries and learn unfamiliar parts of the stack, and a practical mindset for building systems that are secure, reliable, and usable in fast-moving production environments. The systems you build will sit on the critical path of OpenAI’s frontier infrastructure investments and will directly shape how large amounts of compute are brought online - securely, responsibly, and at global scale - underpinning long-lived commitments around privacy, security, and reliability.

You will partner closely with infrastructure, research, and confidential computing initiatives-including novel hardware platforms and emerging deployment models- to make the secure path the easiest path. This role is well suited for engineers who enjoy working across trust services, operating systems, hardware and firmware validation, and infrastructure security, and who are excited by ambiguous, high-impact problems at the boundary of hardware and large-scale systems.

In this role, you will:

- Design, build, and operate components of the Host Assurance platform that establish trust in both bare-metal & VM hosts before they are eligible for production use.

- Help ensure hosts are verifiably trustworthy from delivery and installation through secure bootstrap and readiness to join orchestration systems.

- Build and improve systems such as machine identity, certificate issuance and enrollment, HSM-backed or key-management-backed trust services, host attestation, measurement, and baseline verification tooling.

- Validate delivered hardware and firmware against vendor claims and continuously detect and manage drift over time.

- Eliminate insecure bootstrap patterns while preserving deployment throughput and operational reliability. Partner with provisioning, fleet, and orchestration teams to deliver paved paths where the secure approach is the easiest approach.

- Own software components through implementation, operational readiness, launch, and ongoing operation. Define readiness criteria, validate behavior under load and failure, establish monitoring and actionable alerts, plan staged rollouts and tested recovery procedures, and maintain runbooks. Use production experience to improve reliability and reduce operational burden.

- Participate in production support via oncall rotation.

- Help define observable, testable security properties for host platforms and improve the telemetry and validation needed to enforce them in practice.

- Work across different deployment models and provider boundaries while maintaining a consistent bar for host trust outcomes.
